page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native virtual server configured with 4 shared vCPUs and 24.0 GB of RAM, running on the KVM hypervisor. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. This configuration provides 6.0 GB of memory per core, utilizing 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. The CPU includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and FMA. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate to weak profile, influenced by the shared CPU allocation. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance is in the bottom 25%. However, the PassMark CPU score of 8197.87 and PassMark CPU extended instructions test score of 7060.15 sit in the middle 50%. Memory performance is mixed; small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 411.67 GB/sec, but the PassMark memory score is poor, placing in the bottom 10%.

For application workloads, the server demonstrates average capabilities in data compression, with gzip compression at 25.46 GB/sec and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 37.38 GB/sec. Database and web serving operations are weaker, with Redis SET operations yielding 5.87 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 3.54 GB/sec. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio without demanding sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, lightweight web serving, development environments, and basic text or prompt processing tasks.
